common_name: Bella Sera Daylily (Mauve Purple with Silver Lavender Edge)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Bella Sera is a fragrant 2002 evergreen introduction that reblooms.

directions: Bella Sera, registered by Stamile in 2002, produces mauve purple flowers edged in silver lavender above a green throat on fragrant, evergreen, tetraploid scapes about 30 inches tall that rebloom through an early-to-midseason display. Plant divisions in full sun in rich, well-drained soil, where established clumps can carry roughly 30 buds per scape. It later became a parent, crossed with Unending Melody, of the Award of Merit winner Asheville After Dark.

common_name: Council Fire Daylily (Orange with Red Veins and Eyezone)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Council Fire is a dormant 1995 introduction with a midseason-to-late bloom window.

directions: Council Fire, registered by Roderick in 1995, bears orange flowers etched with red veins and a red eyezone above a green-gold throat, carried on dormant, tetraploid scapes near 30 inches tall during a midseason-to-late bloom window. Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil, dividing congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor. It was later crossed with You Glow Girl to produce the Award of Merit winner Mardi Gras Indian.

common_name: Ginger Twist Daylily (Unusual-Form Pink Orange with Red Band)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Ginger Twist is a dormant, unusual-form 1999 introduction that reblooms.

directions: Ginger Twist, registered by Trimmer in 1999, opens enormous 11-inch unusual-form crispate flowers in pink orange with a red band above a green throat, carried on dormant, tetraploid scapes about 29 inches tall that rebloom through midseason. Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, allowing room for its wide, twisted petals to display fully. It later contributed, crossed with Hankow, to the Award of Merit winner Gryphon Hankow Legacy.

common_name: Hankow Daylily (Red Orange with Scarlet Eyezone)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Hankow is a historic 1939 diploid introduction.

directions: Hankow, registered by Arlow Stout in 1939, is a historic diploid cultivar bearing spreading red-orange flowers with a scarlet eyezone, as described in a 1954 Arvista Gardens catalog listing, on dormant scapes reaching about 42 inches during a midseason display. Plant divisions in full sun in average, well-drained garden soil; this early-twentieth-century introduction predates most modern tetraploid breeding lines. It was later used as a parent, crossed with Ginger Twist, of the Award of Merit winner Gryphon Hankow Legacy.

common_name: Hippopotamus Daylily (Peachy Pink with Lighter Watermark)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Hippopotamus is a fragrant, dormant 2011 introduction that reblooms.

directions: Hippopotamus, registered by Gossard in 2011, bears fragrant, 8-inch peachy pink flowers with a greenish undertone, a lighter watermark, and a greenish-yellow edge above a green throat, held on dormant, tetraploid scapes about 38 inches tall that rebloom from midseason into late season. Plant divisions in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, siting clumps where their broad blooms can be viewed up close. It was later crossed with Wolfman to produce the Award of Merit winner Heavenly New Frontiers.

common_name: Lovely Miss Laucius Daylily (Deep Purple with Lavender Watermark)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun for the richest wine-toned color; Lovely Miss Laucius is a semi-evergreen 2007 introduction that reblooms.

directions: Lovely Miss Laucius, registered by Owen-Pearce in 2007, carries fragrant deep purple flowers nearly 7.5 inches across, marked with a large lavender watermark, on semi-evergreen, tetraploid scapes around 30 inches tall that rebloom through midseason. Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil for the richest wine-toned color. It later became a parent, crossed with Still the One, of the Award of Merit winner MeMe's Merlot.

common_name: Spacecoast Five O'Clock Somewhere Daylily (Dark Red with Lighter Watermark)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in mild-winter gardens where its evergreen foliage persists.

directions: Spacecoast Five O'Clock Somewhere, registered by Kinnebrew-Gossard in 2015, bears fragrant dark red flowers with a lighter watermark and a yellow edge above a yellow-green throat, on evergreen, tetraploid scapes about 31 inches tall that rebloom through an early-season display. Plant divisions in full sun in warm, well-drained garden soil, as this evergreen cultivar performs best where winters stay mild. It was later crossed with Spacecoast Saltwater Taffy to produce Spacecoast Tequila Sunrise.

common_name: Spacecoast Saltwater Taffy Daylily (Deep Red with Yellow-Orange Watermark)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in mild-winter gardens where its evergreen foliage persists.

directions: Spacecoast Saltwater Taffy, registered by Kinnebrew-Gossard in 2015, opens fragrant deep red flowers banded with a yellow-orange watermark and a matching yellow-orange edge, on evergreen, tetraploid scapes near 35 inches tall that rebloom through an early-season display. Plant divisions in full sun in mild-winter gardens where its evergreen foliage persists, in fertile, well-drained soil. It is a sibling cross of Spacecoast Five O'Clock Somewhere, and together the two produced the award-nominated Spacecoast Tequila Sunrise.

common_name: Still the One Daylily (Purple Bitone with Blue-Gray Watermark)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Still the One is a semi-evergreen 2006 introduction that reblooms.

directions: Still the One, registered by Davisson in 2006, bears fragrant purple bitone flowers over 8 inches wide, marked with a blue-gray watermark and a dark purple pencil edge above a wide triangular yellow-to-green throat, on semi-evergreen, tetraploid scapes about 40 inches tall that rebloom from early season. Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, giving its tall scapes room to display above the foliage. It was later crossed with Lovely Miss Laucius to produce the Award of Merit winner MeMe's Merlot.

common_name: Sweet Dixie Daylily (Orange Burgundy with Black Burgundy Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in mild-winter gardens where its evergreen foliage persists.

directions: Sweet Dixie, registered by Bell-Thomas in 2009, bears fragrant orange-burgundy flowers with a black-burgundy eye and matching edge above a neon orange throat, carried on evergreen, tetraploid scapes about 34 inches tall that rebloom through midseason. Plant divisions in full sun in mild-winter gardens where its evergreen foliage persists, in fertile, well-drained soil. It was later crossed with Thin Man to produce the Award of Merit winner Gone with the Wine.

common_name: Unending Melody Daylily (Cream Peach with Wine Purple Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, dividing crowded clumps every three to four years.

directions: Unending Melody, registered by Carpenter-Jablonski in 2000, produces fragrant cream-peach flowers with a wine-purple eye and matching edge above a yellow-green throat, on evergreen, tetraploid scapes about 30 inches tall that carry unusually high bud counts near 45 per scape and rebloom through midseason. Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, and divide crowded clumps every three to four years. It was later crossed with Bella Sera to produce the Award of Merit winner Asheville After Dark.

common_name: Wolfman Daylily (Burgundy Red with Toothy Gold Edge)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Wolfman is a fragrant, dormant 2013 introduction with a compact habit.

directions: Wolfman, registered by Gossard in 2013, bears fragrant burgundy red flowers with a lighter eye above a green throat, edged in gold-to-white teeth, on dormant, tetraploid scapes about 24 inches tall during a midseason-to-late bloom window. Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, where its compact habit and heavily toothed edge are shown off at the front of a border. It was later crossed with Hippopotamus to produce the Award of Merit winner Heavenly New Frontiers.

common_name: You Glow Girl Daylily (Hot Pink with Bubbly Knobbed Edge)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun for the strongest edge texture and color saturation.

directions: You Glow Girl, registered by Selman in 2004, bears fragrant hot pink flowers with a small dark rose eye and a bubbly, hooked and knobbed edge above a gold-green heart-shaped throat, on dormant, tetraploid scapes about 30 inches tall during a midseason display. Plant divisions in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil for the strongest edge texture and color saturation. It was later crossed with Council Fire to produce the Award of Merit winner Mardi Gras Indian.
